verification.note: Tables 3 to 10 parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber table extraction, specimen columns assigned from the header cells) and compared cell by cell with page images rendered at 2.6x; number resistant over number tested was also recomputed for every cell and all differences over 1 point are noted on the cell. Chart values (Figures 9, 11, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22) are printed data labels from the text layer: each label was assigned to the bar whose end it sits next to on the same row, the series from the legend swatch colours, and the bar length measured against the axis ticks agreed with the label within 0.1 point for every bar; 0% labels of zero-length bars were placed by row position; every chart was also checked by eye on the rendered page. Page numbers are PDF page numbers, which equal the printed page numbers in this report.

sources.notes: First annual report of AARSNET, the Assam state AMR surveillance network under NCDC (nodal centre Gauhati Medical College and Hospital, 12 government medical colleges): 14,179 priority-pathogen isolates from 13,369 unique patients in 2025 (the Discussion gives different totals: 14,346 reported, 11,834 and 13,299 after deduplication). Values are % resistant as printed. Genus-level organisms as printed. Pus aspirate (aspirated purulent material from a closed infected site; pus and wound swabs excluded) is mapped to deep; other sterile body fluids (CSF, pleural, peritoneal, synovial, pericardial) to sterile; IPD to ward. Location rows pool all specimens and carry no n (not printed with the charts); Table 4 location counts are recorded as counts. Several location figures do not reconcile with the specimen tables (S. aureus linezolid, Pseudomonas gentamicin, E. coli co-trimoxazole), see cell notes. Table 4 location counts do not sum to the Table 3 totals for Klebsiella (2,861 against 2,890), Pseudomonas (1,121 against 1,065) and S. aureus (1,684 against 1,711).
issues: Lead 2026-09-26: four figures the report contradicts (Enterococcus urine ciprofloxacin, E. coli urine co-trimoxazole, Pseudomonas gentamicin in the OPD and IPD chart) are marked as conflicts: shown with a caution, never pooled or used by reasoning.

Second reader 2026-09-26: the seeded sample of 117 of 469 cells (every table and chart) and all 21 table row n re-read on page images (scale 2.6 to 3.5) and compared with the file: 0 errors. Beyond the sample, all 233 table cells (Tables 5 to 10, value and number tested, resistant count recomputed) were compared with an independent parse of the text layer (specimen columns assigned from the header cells, since their order differs between tables), all 236 chart values (Figure 9 OSBF series, Figures 11, 14, 16, 18, 20 and 22) were re-assigned to bars independently (series from the legend swatch colour, every label within 0.6 point of its bar length, 0% labels of zero-length bars placed by slot position and checked by eye), and all 46 counts (Tables 3 and 4) were re-read: 0 discrepancies, nothing corrected.

Cells not kept by the validator, all printed that way: Enterococcus blood nitrofurantoin 40%R (42 of 104); Enterococcus urine ciprofloxacin 49%R with 730 resistant of 361 tested (no nt recorded, on purpose); E. coli urine co-trimoxazole 0%R (1 of 2,979); E. coli pus fosfomycin 3%R (5 of 169) and nitrofurantoin 31%R (10 of 32); E. coli blood fosfomycin 1%R (1 of 88); Figure 20 Pseudomonas gentamicin OPD 0% (zero-length bar in the OPD slot) and IPD 1%. The validator reports no count-table mismatch.

For the lead (not changed): E. coli pus cefuroxime is printed 86%R but its printed counts give 224 of 273 = 82%; by the brief that is a conflict, the file has it as a cell note only. Klebsiella blood colistin printed 0.009%R (2 of 207 = 1.0%) is likewise a note only.
Lead 2026-09-26: E. coli pus aspirate cefuroxime (printed 86% resistant, its counts give 224 of 273 = 82%) recorded as a conflict, as the conflict rule requires for gaps of a point or more.

sources.notes: Das PP et al., J Pure Appl Microbiol 2023;17(3):1591-1604. Assam Medical College & Hospital, Dibrugarh (institution-wide, AMRSN/ICMR site). Study period Oct 2018-Mar 2021. Text-extracted with pymupdf (Read tool could not render PDF; poppler not installed). All susceptibility data reported as %RESISTANT (R%) in Table 2 (Gram-negatives) and Table 3 (Gram-positives); every cell converted to %S = 100 - R with from_R:true. Table 2 organisms labelled Klebsiella spp./Proteus spp./Enterobacter spp. mapped to K. pneumoniae/P. mirabilis/E. cloacae with per-cell notes (Klebsiella predominantly K. pneumoniae per abstract). Citrobacter kept as genus. n values taken from Table 2 headers (Acinetobacter n=687, Pseudomonas n=646); note text on p.9 gives slightly different NFGNB counts (A. baumannii n=550, P. aeruginosa n=590). Cefepime, Tobramycin (except Pseudomonas), Minocycline (except Acinetobacter) etc. were ND (not done) for several organisms and omitted. Colistin: MIC-tested on only 261 pooled GN isolates, all susceptible (not organism-specific, so not added per organism). S. aureus vancomycin s=100 added because text states VRSA not detected. MRSA 44.7% = cefoxitin resistance. VRE overall 1

sources.notes: Source: Panigrahi et al., Cureus 2025;17(10):e94006 (KIMS Bhubaneswar). PDF read via PyMuPDF text extraction (pdftoppm/pdftotext unavailable). Data taken from Table 2 (page 10), which prints Sensitive/Intermediate/Resistant counts and percentages for each of 13 drugs across the whole study population and 4 subgroups (ICU, non-ICU, CAI, HAI). I extracted the overall Total (n=7,942) Sensitive % values as printed (%S only; Intermediate not added). Values match the abstract/text (tigecycline 74.79%S, gentamicin 39.45%S, meropenem 34.34%S, piptazo 32.44%S). Note the scope hint 'cipro 78.4%R' corresponds to the Resistant column (6,227, 78.40%R); the reported %S for ciprofloxacin is 19.08% (I:2.50%), so no %R conversion was needed as %S is printed directly. CPS = cefoperazone-sulbactam mapped to non-canonical token 'cefoperazonesulbactam' (distinct from plain cefoperazone). Only organism studied is K. pneumoniae; other Klebsiella species excluded by authors. Subgroup rows (ICU/non-ICU/CAI/HAI) also available in Table 2 but only the overall pooled figures extracted here. VITEK 2, CLSI 2022 breakpoints.

sources.notes: Source: Poddar et al., Cureus 18(3):e104772 (2026), KIMS Bhubaneswar, Odisha; retrospective sterile-body-fluid antibiogram, Jan 2021-Dec 2022. 2307 samples, 291 isolates (12.6% positive); GPC 54%, S. aureus most common (92/291), MRSA 48.9%; K. pneumoniae top GNB (40), E. coli (27), Acinetobacter (24), Pseudomonas (19). All susceptibility data are presented ONLY as unlabeled bar charts (Fig 1 = Gram-positive: S. aureus, CONS, Enterococcus; Fig 2 = Gram-negative: K. pneumoniae, E. coli, Pseudomonas spp., Acinetobacter spp.) plus narrative sentences. There are NO numeric susceptibility tables. Method: rendered figure pages with PyMuPDF at 6x, calibrated the y-axis from detected tick-label centers (Fig 2: 0%=y1383, 100%=y368; Fig 1 baseline y1504), then extracted each bar's top and mid-bar color programmatically. Color->drug map validated by matching extracted values to the paper's own text (Acinetobacter imipenem 41.9 vs 'imipenem 41%', gentamicin 41.5 vs 'aminoglycosides 41%', cotrimoxazole 36.8 vs '37.5%', ciprofloxacin 36.8 vs '38%'; E. coli ciprofloxacin 10.8 vs 'ciprofloxacin resistance high 90%'; Pseudomonas ceftazidime 20.9 vs '21%', ciprofloxacin 9.9 vs '10-11%'). Values are %
issues: Staph aureus text-derived cells (linezolid 95.65, dapto 95, TGC 92, VA/TEI 90.21): the paper states these for 'Staphylococcus spp.' collectively (Fig 1 has separate S. aureus and CoNS bar groups). Assigning them specifically to S. aureus is a reasonable but not certain mapping; the 95.65% 'highest' value could belong to either Staph group.

Pseudomonas amikacin s=20.9 is read as LOWER than meropenem/cefepime (25.9), but the text explicitly says Pseudomonas showed 'highest sensitivity to amikacin, followed by carbapenems' — i.e., amikacin should exceed the carbapenems. Bar-read ordering is inconsistent with the text; value is approximate so not force-corrected, but flag for review.

Klebsiella ampicillin s=41.9 (bar read) is clinically implausible since K. pneumoniae is intrinsically ampicillin-resistant (expected ~0%); cannot confirm from the rendered bar chart. Possible misread of the AMP bar.
Oxacillin s=51.1 is a valid 100-R conversion from MRSA 48.9% (45/92); direction correct.

All remaining Gram-negative per-drug numbers are pixel reads off Figure 2 bar chart and cannot be independently confirmed to the stated decimal precision; they are appropriately flagged approx and are broadly consistent with the text ranges (amikacin 41-63%, carbapenems 40-60%, E. coli cipro ~10%).

verification.note: Part 1: Part A of the report (chapters 1 to 3). Every table was parsed from the text layer with pdfplumber, every cell was checked arithmetically (printed n/N against the printed %), and every value was then compared by eye against page renders at scale 2.2 to 2.4 (wide tables cut into halves or thirds). Source inconsistencies found this way are recorded as printed with notes (M. morganii urine amikacin, A. baumannii ward colistin, S. maltophilia ceftazidime and others). Part 2: Part B (chapters 4 to 9). Every extracted table was parsed from the PDF text layer by script (pdfplumber tables and text lines, no retyping) and then compared value by value by eye against page images rendered at scale 2.2 to 3.2 and cropped by column group: Tables 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 5.1 to 5.9, 6.1, 6.2, 6.4 to 6.15, 6.17, 7.1 to 7.4, 8.3, 9.27 to 9.29 and 9.39 to 9.41 (Table 9.44, also compared, is excluded: see excluded). sources.notes: ICMR AMRSN 2024, part A: Enterobacterales (chapter 2) and non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli (chapter 3), plus isolation counts from chapter 1. 99,027 culture-positive isolates from the network's tertiary-care centres. Enterobacterales rows are 'all specimens except urine and faeces' (spec nonurine) by location, urine rows are all locations; non-fermenter rows are 'all samples (except faeces)' (spec all) by location and by specimen. Colistin figures are percent intermediate. CR and CS rows are carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets. Counts: Table 1.3 by location (all specimens) and Tables 1.5, 1.10, 1.13 and 1.17 by specimen (all locations); the two sets overlap, so their sum is not an isolate total. CoNS counts are the Table 1.13 CoNS total; Enterococcus spp. counts are the unspeciated group of Table 1.17 (E. faecalis and E. faecium are counted separately). Part B of the ICMR AMRSN 2024 annual report (merged by the lead with Part A, chapters 1 to 3): typhoidal Salmonella, diarrhoeal pathogens, staphylococci and enterococci, fungi, S. pneumoniae (invasive, Table 8.3) and ICU HAI surveillance susceptibility (cohort "hai"). Cells printed as "(-)" (too few isolates) are left out. Fungal tables print S, I/SDD and R; only S is recorded. Several fungal percentages are printed 0.1 above the count ratio (e.g. 17/18 printed 94.5); recorded as printed. Isolates come from tertiary care hospitals; the report says the data do not reflect community AMR (p5). The ICMR network report for 2024 (21 regional centres; 99,027 culture-positive isolates). Extracted in two parts by table chapter and merged; the transcribed national summary used before this is superseded.

Every susceptibility table was parsed from the PDF text layer with pdfplumber (no retyping), every cell was checked arithmetically (printed n/N against the printed %), and every value was then compared by eye against page renders at scale 2.2 to 2.6 (wide tables cut into two or three crops): Tables 2.7 to 2.9, 2.11 to 2.13, 2.16, 2.18 to 2.20, 3.1 to 3.5, 3.14, 3.19, 3.20, 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 4.5, 4.7, 4.8, 4.10 and 4.11. Source inconsistencies are recorded as printed with conflict entries or notes (colistin in Tables 2.11 to 2.13 and 2.16, the repeated colistin cell of Table 3.1, S. maltophilia OPD levofloxacin, denominators above the column n in Tables 3.19 and 3.20, sample-wise n in Tables 4.2 and 4.5). CR and CS rows are carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets. The sample-wise non-fermenter tables (4.2, 4.5) print an n per specimen that matches the numbers tested, well below the isolate counts of Table 1.10. sources.notes: Source: Gautam et al, Indian J Med Res 2019;149:208-215 (ICMR multi-centric ESBL study, 4 tertiary centres: AIIMS Delhi, PGIMER Chandigarh, CMC Vellore, JIPMER Puducherry; Oct 2014-Mar 2016). Study covers ONLY E. coli (341 isolates) and K. pneumoniae (304 isolates) — no P. aeruginosa, A. baumannii, S. aureus, or Enterococcus. Method: Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion, CLSI. Table II reports % SUSCEPTIBLE by centre; Table III reports % RESISTANT (n/N) split by ESBL-producer vs non-ESBL. I derived OVERALL susceptibility by pooling Table III ESBL + non-ESBL resistant counts per drug (s = 100 - pooled %R, from_R:true for all pooled cells). Colistin values taken directly from the printed overall figures in the Results text (E. coli 99% = 271/274; K. pneumoniae 98% = 229/234), not from R. CAVEAT: Table III denominators (e.g. 167+202=369 for E. coli, 98+126=224 for K. pneumoniae) exceed stated collection totals of 341/304, likely reflecting drug-specific tested subsets/classification; per-drug pooled %R is nevertheless computed directly from printed n/N. Individual per-centre susceptibility values are available in Table II if centre-level breakdown is preferred. ESBL prevalence context: CDT dete

sources.notes: Ninth NARS-Net annual report: 62 sentinel sites (medical college laboratories) in 34 states and UTs, priority bacterial pathogens January to December 2025 (first isolate per patient). All figures are percent resistant (intermediate counted as not resistant). Specimens: pus aspirate (PA) is shown as pus; other sterile body fluids (OSBF) as sterile body fluids, although NARS-Net OSBF also includes CSF and broncho-alveolar lavage. Table rows combine all location types (set all). Location rows (outpatient, ward, ICU) come from bar charts with printed data labels; the report adds emergency department isolates to inpatient wards (shown here as wards). Cells marked x in the source (drug not in the panel for that specimen) are absent. Salmonella Typhi and Paratyphi A are reported separately; pefloxacin has no drug key. Candida from blood (997 isolates, fungal NRL) has no susceptibility table, so none is recorded (see excluded). The report warns that specimens come mostly from patients not responding to first-line antibiotics, which may skew resistance upward.

sources.notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 30 (1) and 31 (1), two years combined (January 2023 to December 2024), 8 pages. Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus/tissue; body fluids; respiratory specimens): organism bar charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates, legend counts and an "others" list) and Gram-positive (GPC) and Gram-negative (GNB) percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus (printed "Pus / Tissue", pus and tissue reported together), sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory. Rows printed "Staphylococcus spp." (pus: "Staphylococci spp.") are separate from Staph. aureus and are recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci, as the 2011 edition labels the same row "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)". Combined columns: "Cefoxitin/Oxacillin" is recorded under oxacillin, "Imipenem/Meropenem" (blood and body fluid GNB tables) under meropenem, and "Glycopeptides" under vancomycin (vancomycin and teicoplanin reported as one figure; the 2011 edition heads the same column "Vancomycin/Teicoplanin"); each such cell says so in its note. The "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded. Blood S. pneumoniae: penicillin and ceftriaxone hold the non-meningitis breakpoint columns; the meningitis-breakpoint values are in the cell notes. Urine and pus imipenem is printed "*Imipenem" with a footnote advising an alternative method before reporting Vitek 2 imipenem results for Proteus, Morganella and Providencia (noted on the Proteus cells). Colistin is not reported: the newsletter states that CLSI has had no susceptible category for colistin in Gram-negative bacteria since 2020. Fungal isolates are counted in the charts but their susceptibility data were deferred to the next issue. Isolate numbers: the charts and the tables disagree by one isolate for 10 organism strata (blood ICU E. coli; urine ward E. coli and E. faecalis; urine ICU E. coli and P. aeruginosa; pus OPD K. pneumoniae; pus ward and body fluid OPD coagulase-negative staphylococci; body fluid ward E. coli and K. pneumoniae); each is recorded as printed and noted on its row. The body fluid ICU "others" list sums to 49 against "Others-50". Some percentages are not what rounding gives for the row's n (urine ICU Proteus n=12 prints cefuroxime 41 where 5/12 is 41.7, which suggests truncation), and a few match no count of the row's isolates at all (body fluid OPD Enterobacter n=13, cefepime 66; respiratory ward S. pneumoniae n=21, penicillin and ceftriaxone 97): per-drug tested numbers are not printed; all are recorded as printed. Organism counts: every legend and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla", "Serratia marscecens", "Elizebethkingia meninseptica", "Sphinmonas paucimobilis", "Neisseria norrhoeae", "L.monocytogenes"); "Salmonella entertidis" is recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella and "Serratia odorifera" as Serratia spp.; entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Page 1 and 8 (case report, publications, highlights) and page 7 (antimicrobial consumption) are not susceptibility tables.

sources.notes: Earlier UPUMS Saifai hospital antibiogram (23 pages, all charts). Other samples means all samples except blood and urine (per the report): superficial infections, lower respiratory tract, deep infections, sterile sites, CSF and other sample types (1018, 291, 129, 78, 16 and 307 isolates in Section A). There is no specimen key for that mix, so it is recorded as pus with specimen_as_printed and each row's note gives the specimen mix of its location: superficial infections are 430 of 541 OPD, 565 of 1011 ward and only 23 of 288 ICU positive samples in this group (the ICU group is mostly LRT and other sample types). Also recorded: the carbapenem-resistant (CR) and carbapenem-susceptible (CS) subset tables (Section B V) for Acinetobacter, P. aeruginosa, K. pneumoniae and E. coli from all specimens except faeces (spec all), whose colistin figures rest on 1 to 24 selected isolates (mostly marked as broth microdilution in selected MDR isolates). sources.notes: Antibiogram section (printed pages 6 to 17, PDF pages 14 to 25) of the SKNMC and GH Antibiotic Policy for Hospital, Version 2.1, dated 15 December 2024 (implementation 1 January 2025). Only organism-level lists are recorded: the 11 'Pseudomonas (n=...)' lines, one per box, and the Respiratory-ICU Gram-positive list, which that box attributes entirely to Staphylococcus aureus (prevalence 100% of the Gram-positive cocci). The pooled Gram-positive and Gram-negative lists mix several organisms and are left out (see excluded), so this file does not give E. coli, Klebsiella, Acinetobacter or enterococcal figures even though the boxes name them. Syndromes are recorded as specimens: BSI as blood, UTI as urine, respiratory as respiratory, SSTI as pus. IPD is recorded as wards because each syndrome has a separate ICU box. There is no BSI-OPD box. The data period is printed only as 2024 without months; since the policy is dated 15 December 2024 it cannot include all of December 2024. The Pseudomonas n printed on each line does not match the Pseudomonas share given in the prevalence column (a percentage of the Gram-negative group), so it may count only tested or only P. aeruginosa isolates; recorded as printed. Pseudomonas lines print 'Pipracillin', recorded as piperacillin. Page numbers are PDF pages (printed page number plus 8).
